candidate.answerReason: If each drawer held at most one object, there could not be more objects than drawers. Therefore at least one drawer must hold two or more.

methods.label: Compare objects with available drawers
methods.explanation: With more objects than drawers, putting at most one object in each drawer cannot fit all the objects. At least one drawer must therefore contain at least 2 objects. This is the simplest case of the pigeonhole principle. The answer is A.
methods.levelReason: Comparing the object count with the drawer count is the elementary Grade 6 pigeonhole principle.
